text:
elaine: quick heads-up — we're seeing very high first-request tails for models split into many tiny safetensors shards. index-first warmup is safe but S3 list/stat latency is killing p99. need tradeoffs and a loader plan.

mike: saw that in prod for a couple customers yesterday. index-first = correctness, but the per-shard stat/lists add 100-400ms. dedicated nodes pre-warming helps, hosted does not.

arjun: thought: add a tiny footer (embedded index) in safetensors that holds offsets+crc for tensors. single small read of last ~4KB would give us O(1) index lookup after shard download.

sash: embedding is elegant but breaks current format compatibility and forces model owners to rewrite artifacts. also increases upload cost when repacking.

elaine: can we be dual-mode? embedded footer optional. loader: check embedded footer first, then external .meta/.index, then on-demand probing, then stream-decode fallback.

arjun: loader flow sketch:
```
# attempt small tail read -> parse footer.magic
if footer present: use embedded index
else: fetch small /model/path.safetensors.meta from CDN
if meta missing: do windowed range reads (8MB windows) in parallel to build index (rate-limited)
if that times out: fall back to streaming decode
```

mike: important: when building index from range probes, avoid single-tensor HEADs. batch into window reads and parse multiple tensors per window. tune window size by median tensor size.

elaine: add a prefetch budget per-model to limit probe_bytes. also TTL cache the .meta on the loader side keyed by content-hash to avoid staleness.

arjun: noted. also propose a WeightSource API change: resolve_shard(uri, prefer_embedded=true, max_probe_bytes=2097152, timeout_ms=300) -> returns {kind:index|meta|scan|stream, index_blob_or_handle}. callers can pick tighter budgets.

sash: another constraint: gzipped artifacts. range reads on gzipped objects are essentially broken because compression boundaries; we should require .meta or embedded footer for gzipped shards and discourage gzipping for production checkpoints. upload pipeline should validate.

mike: +1. For CDN/backing store: require a small .meta on publish for gzipped artifacts. cost is tiny, benefit large for tail latency.

arjun: alternative low-cost idea: put a tiny fingerprint blob in object metadata (S3 user metadata) pointing to the small index stored at /meta/<hash>. but S3 metadata size is limited; use it only as a hint.

elaine: operational metrics to emit from loader: index_lookup_type (embedded|meta|scan|stream), index_build_time_ms, bytes_probed_before_indexed, fallback_to_stream_count, index_cache_hit, meta_stale_errors, p99_latency_impact.

mike: Dedicated should hotstart pinned models' indexes during node startup to avoid first-request storms. Hosted can do adaptive prefetch for models with rising qps.

sash: parallelism safety: start with conservative 4 parallel probe workers with exponential backoff on 429/5xx. instrument per-bucket throttling and adapt.

elaine: uploader changes: require .meta for gzipped; recommend non-gzipped for production. provide an optional tool to retrofit existing model buckets with .meta computed from shards.

arjun: gotchas: quantized formats with dense packing make offsets less predictable; window heuristics must support variable-length tensors. also need to parse some header signatures to detect packing.

mike: add per-model probe budget so a single large model doesn't blow egress. and pin indexes by content-hash to avoid stale cached index after new upload.

ops: deployment note — we need a migration plan. if we accept embedded footers, we must support both old and new shards for at least 6 months and have a tool to add .meta to existing artifacts.

elaine: proposed action items:
- arjun: prototype embedded-footer read + loader preference logic (2w)
- sash: add .meta emit and uploader validation (1w)
- mike: implement index metrics + hotstart prefetch hook for Dedicated (1w)
- ops: canary on a few orgs to measure p50/p95/p99 changes after proto (2w after protos)

sash: i'll draft a compatibility guide and a retrofitter to generate .meta files for buckets.

elaine: final open question: should loader try to parallelize index-build aggressively or be conservative?

mike: be conservative initially — 4 workers with backoff and adapt by observing S3 429/slow responses. also expose a per-bucket concurrency cap.

arjun: +1. also fail fast to stream-decode if we see high throttling to avoid cascading stalls.

elaine: great. i'll convert this into a short RFC follow-up comparing index-on-read (meta), embedded-footer, and indexless scan with clear metrics to hit. will post draft to #eng-ml.

mike: :thumbsup:

sash: :rocket:
